title: Gold Demand Trends: Q2 2026
gist: Total gold demand including OTC was flat y/y at 1,269t in Q2 2026 while the LBMA PM price averaged US$4,506.29/oz (-8% from the Q1 record, +37% y/y), pushing H1 demand value to a record US$380bn. The composition rotated hard: ETFs swung to a 45t outflow and bar/coin normalised to 307t, while central banks rebounded to 289t (+411% q/q) and OTC surged to 327.1t; jewellery volumes fell to a post-pandemic low of 278t.

themes.theme: Headline demand and record H1 value

insights.claim: Total gold demand including OTC was unchanged y/y at 1,269t in Q2 2026, taking first-half demand to 2,522t (+2% y/y) with a record value of US$380bn.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Volume is flat but value is at a record, so the gold complex's revenue pool (miners, refiners, retailers) is expanding on price rather than tonnage — favour price-levered equities over volume-levered ones.
insights.quote: Total gold demand, including OTC, was unchanged y/y at 1,269t in Q2. This took demand for the first half year to 2,522t (+2% y/y), with a record value of US$380bn.
insights.locator: Demand steadies in Q2 as price softens

insights.claim: Excluding OTC, reported gold demand fell to 941.8t in Q2 2026, down 7% q/q and down 14% y/y, with the gap versus flat headline demand filled by OTC and other demand of 327.1t (+34% q/q, +91% y/y).
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The marginal buyer has moved off-exchange and is unobservable in weekly ETF data — monitoring only visible flows will understate real demand and mislead on price support.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly gold supply and demand by sector, tonnes

themes.theme: Investment flows: ETF outflows versus OTC and retail

insights.claim: Gold ETFs and similar products swung to a 45t outflow in Q2 2026 (-44.8t), reversing inflows of 62.4t in Q1 2026 and 171.1t in Q2 2025.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: ETF flows have flipped from tailwind to headwind; treat weekly ETF holdings as the fastest read on whether Western financial demand re-engages.
insights.quote: Gold ETFs came under selling pressure in Q2 (-45t).
insights.locator: Gold ETFs came under selling pressure

insights.claim: The World Gold Council attributes Q2 2026 gold ETF outflows to weaker gold prices and, particularly in North America, upward adjustments to both inflation and interest rate expectations alongside a strengthening US dollar.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The stated driver set — real-rate expectations plus the dollar — gives a direct macro trigger list: a dovish repricing or dollar rollover should restart North American ETF buying.
insights.quote: Moderate outflows were in response to weaker gold prices and, particularly in North America, upward adjustments to both inflation and interest rate expectations alongside a strengthening US dollar.
insights.locator: Moderate outflows were in response to weaker

insights.claim: Bar and coin investment held steady y/y at 307t in Q2 2026 (307.1t, -3% y/y, -36% q/q from 476.8t in Q1), which the World Gold Council describes as a return to more typical levels after two extraordinarily strong quarters.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Retail physical demand normalising rather than collapsing means the price floor from bar/coin buyers is intact; a further leg down here would be the real warning sign.
insights.quote: This signalled a return to more typical levels of buying following two extraordinarily strong quarters.
insights.locator: Bar and coin investment held steady y/y

insights.claim: Within Q2 2026 physical retail demand, bars accounted for 247.8t (-1% y/y) while official coins fell to 33.5t, down 16% y/y and down 35% q/q from 51.8t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Coin weakness versus resilient bars points to fading small-ticket Western retail while larger-denomination buying persists — relevant for mints and retail bullion dealer volumes.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly gold supply and demand by sector, tonnes

insights.claim: Total reported investment demand collapsed to 262.2t in Q2 2026, down 51% q/q from 539.2t and down 46% y/y from 486.8t, as ETF outflows compounded lower bar and coin buying.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The halving of visible investment demand in a quarter when price held above US$4,500/oz shows how much of the bid has migrated to OTC and central banks — a fragile-looking but so far effective support structure.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly gold supply and demand by sector, tonnes

insights.claim: Central banks and other institutions bought 288.9t of gold in Q2 2026, up 411% q/q from 56.5t in Q1 and up 62% y/y from 177.9t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The official-sector bid is back at trend after a one-quarter air pocket; this is the most price-insensitive source of demand and underwrites downside in the gold price.
insights.quote: Central banks made significant gold purchases in Q2 (289t).
insights.locator: Central banks made significant gold purchases

insights.claim: The World Gold Council says the weak Q1 2026 central bank figure of 56.5t reflected a downward revision to its own data, and that Q2 buying recovered sharply to the lofty levels typical of the last four years.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Do not extrapolate single soft quarters in WGC central bank data — the series is revision-prone, so trade the four-year trend rather than the quarterly print.
insights.quote: After a notable Q1 slowdown following a downward revision to our data, buying among this cohort recovered sharply to the lofty levels that have been typical in the last four years.
insights.locator: After a notable Q1 slowdown following a downward revision

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects central banks to remain on course for another strong year of gold buying in 2026, although likely lower than 2025.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A strong-but-decelerating official bid caps the upside impulse from this channel; watch monthly IMF/central bank reporting for whether the run-rate undershoots that guidance.
insights.quote: Central banks remain on course for another strong year, although likely lower than 2025.
insights.locator: Outlook

insights.claim: Gold jewellery consumption fell to 278t in Q2 2026 (278.2t, -17% y/y, -5% q/q), the lowest quarterly volume since the pandemic.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Physical jewellery offtake is no longer a demand engine — jewellery retailers face volume deflation even as their revenue per gram rises.
insights.quote: Jewellery demand fell to its lowest quarterly volume since the pandemic (278t), as high gold prices and broader inflationary pressures continued to constrain affordability.
insights.locator: Jewellery demand fell to its lowest quarterly volume

insights.claim: Despite the volume decline, spending on gold jewellery rose 14% y/y to US$40bn in Q2 2026, which the World Gold Council reads as confirmation of gold's continued importance in share of wallet.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Consumers are paying more for less metal — jewellery chains with pricing power and value-added margins can grow revenue through a tonnage downturn.
insights.quote: In comparison, spending on gold jewellery was up 14% y/y at US$40bn, confirming gold’s continued importance in share of wallet.
insights.locator: In comparison, spending on gold jewellery was up

insights.claim: Jewellery fabrication fell to 310.3t in Q2 2026, down 12% y/y and 7% q/q, running above consumption of 278.2t and leaving 32.1t of jewellery inventory build.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Fabricators are still producing ahead of consumer offtake, so trade-channel destocking is a live risk to next-quarter fabrication demand.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly gold supply and demand by sector, tonnes

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects jewellery volumes to remain under pressure from high gold prices through the second half of 2026.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: No mean-reversion is expected in jewellery tonnage, so the demand mix stays investment-led and therefore more macro-sensitive and more volatile.
insights.quote: Jewellery volumes will likely remain under pressure from high gold prices.
insights.locator: Outlook

themes.theme: Technology demand and the AI offset

insights.claim: Technology usage of gold firmed slightly to 80t in Q2 2026 (80.4t, +2% y/y, -2% q/q) as AI-related demand offset weakness in the consumer electronics market.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: AI hardware build-out is now a visible marginal driver of industrial gold offtake — a small tonnage category, but a clean read on AI capex bleeding into materials demand.
insights.quote: Technology usage of gold again firmed slightly (80t) as AI-related demand offset weakness in the consumer electronics market.
insights.locator: Technology usage of gold again firmed slightly

insights.claim: Electronics gold demand rose 4% y/y to 68.3t in Q2 2026, while other industrial use fell 7% y/y to 10.1t and dentistry fell 6% y/y to 1.9t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Electronics is the only growing industrial sub-segment; use it as a corroborating high-frequency signal on semiconductor and AI-server packaging volumes.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly gold supply and demand by sector, tonnes

themes.theme: Supply: mine output steady, recycling falls

insights.claim: Total gold supply held steady at 1,269t in Q2 2026 (1,268.9t, flat y/y, +1% q/q), as a 2% y/y increase in mine production to 965.6t offset a 6% y/y decline in recycling to 326.1t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Supply is effectively inelastic near record prices, meaning price is being set almost entirely by the demand mix rather than by new metal.
insights.quote: Total gold supply held steady at 1,269t in Q2. A 2% y/y increase in mine production offset a 6% y/y decline in recycling as lower q/q gold prices discouraged selling of old gold jewellery.
insights.locator: Highlights

insights.claim: Recycled gold supply fell 13% q/q to 326.1t in Q2 2026 because lower q/q gold prices discouraged selling of old gold jewellery.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Scrap supply is highly price-reflexive, so any renewed price spike should be met by a fast recycling response that damps the rally.
insights.locator: Highlights

insights.claim: Net producer hedging was negative at -22.8t in Q2 2026, extending a run of de-hedging that included -25.8t in Q2 2025 and -22.1t in Q1 2026.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Miners are buying back hedges rather than locking in record prices — bullish positioning signal from the producers themselves, but it leaves their earnings fully exposed to a price drawdown.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly gold supply and demand by sector, tonnes

insights.claim: The World Gold Council sees only modest growth potential from both mine production and recycling for the remainder of 2026.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Constrained supply growth means demand-side surprises translate more directly into price, supporting a long-bias into any demand catalyst.
insights.quote: We see only modest growth potential from mine production and recycling.
insights.locator: Outlook

insights.claim: The LBMA (PM) gold price averaged US$4,506.29/oz in Q2 2026, 8% below the Q1 2026 record average of US$4,872.9/oz but 37% above the Q2 2025 average of US$3,280.4/oz.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A first quarterly average decline after a parabolic run defines the key technical level: sustained trade below the ~US$4,500 average is where retail and ETF demand assumptions get retested.
insights.quote: The LBMA (PM) gold price averaged US$4,506.29/oz in Q2. The price was 8% lower than the Q1 record, but 37% higher than the average from Q2 2025.
insights.locator: Highlights

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects investment to remain the primary driver of gold demand growth through the second half of 2026, supported increasingly by OTC activity and Asian buying.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The bull case now rests on opaque OTC and Asian flows rather than Western ETFs — position for gold strength that may not show up in the usual Western flow trackers.
insights.quote: We expect investment to remain the primary driver of demand growth through the second half, supported increasingly by OTC activity and Asian buying.
insights.locator: Outlook
